title: The Crow Counsel
text: A parliament of crows sits in judgement on a dead oak, row on row, black, glossy and grave. One old bird with a white eye presides. They caw at whoever lags at the back of the line, harsh and accusing, as if the verdict is already in.

options.label: The slowest stands before the crows' court, and awaits their verdict.

outcomes.text: They judge the laggard worthy. The white-eyed one shows them a shortcut.
They judge the laggard food and fall on them, beaks first.

options.label: Scatter their parliament. No crow sits in judgement on your House.

outcomes.text: They go, cawing outrage, only to return with friends, who have friends of their own.

options.label: Offer them something shiny, to buy their good opinion.

outcomes.text: They caw approval and leave you be. The old one keeps the coin.
